info.description: Static analysis, auto-fix, and AI-assisted review for Power Automate Desktop flows.
info.title: PAD Analyzer API

get.description: Returns the audit trail (logins, settings changes, admin actions), newest first. GET /api/admin/audit/actions lists the action values.

parameters.description: Only events by this user ID, or whose subject is this user (sign-ins, failed sign-ins, lockouts)
parameters.name: userId

get.description: Returns every audit action string the server can emit, so the admin filter offers the full set instead of a hand-maintained subset.

post.description: Copies flows, settings and chat conversations from a legacy filesystem-backed server's data directory (PAD_DATA_DIR) into the database (admin only, cloud mode). Idempotent and non-blocking; the status result lists what is not migrated. Users are not migrated, so flows whose recorded owner is absent here are assigned to the admin who starts the run (reported as FlowsAdopted).

get.description: Returns the status/result of the most recent data migration (admin only).

handleAdminSystemHealth returns a structured per-subsystem health breakdown. Admin-only (the public /readyz is the orchestrator-facing verdict). Reuses the same probes as readiness but reports each independently rather than collapsing to one pass/fail, and does NOT apply the consecutive-failure smoothing — an admin querying health wants the live picture, not a flap-dampened one.
Returns one page of registered users, newest first, with the number of users matching the filters (total). Only available to system admins.

parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring of the email or display name
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: Only this role: admin, member, viewer, guest, or none (accounts without a valid role)
parameters.name: role

400.description: Invalid limit, offset, q or role

get.description: Counts every registered user by role (admin, member, viewer, guest, none) and by state (unverified email, locked out) for the admin overview. Only available to system admins.

put.description: Changes the role of the user with the given ID (admin only).

post.description: Runs all enabled analysis rules on the current flow document.

handleAnalyzeRaw analyzes raw PAD flow text WITHOUT requiring a pre-stored flow, so CI pipelines and wrappers can POST flow text and get findings back in one call — no library upload, no Go CLI install. Works in both modes (auth via PAT in cloud; open in local). Body: {files, name, format?} where format is "json" (default: the analysis report), "sarif" (SARIF 2.1.0), "junit" (JUnit XML) or "csv"; those three are sent as an attachment named pad-analysis.<ext>. At most 50 files and 2048 KB in total. Nothing is persisted.

200.description: Analysis report (json), or the SARIF, JUnit or CSV document

400.description: Bad Request (no files, unknown format, parse failure)

413.description: Too many files or payload too large

post.summary: Clear the baseline for a flow
Compare current analysis against the baseline
Get the baseline snapshot for a flow
Set the current analysis as the baseline
Add a comment to a finding

post.description: Runs one unsaved rule, checked strictly, against a flow and returns the findings it would produce. The body is {rule, flowId} and nothing else; a rule the strict check refuses is a 400 with details.field ("rule.<field>") and details.reason.
post.summary: Test a candidate custom rule against a flow

post.description: Validates custom-rule JSON (an array, one rule with an id, or {"rules": either}) strictly, without installing it. Each entry reports valid, its first error with field and reason, and every problem (problems; warning: true for one the rule runs with). A malformed document is a 400.

JUnit XML report of the flow's analysis (CI test-report viewers), sent as the attachment pad-analysis.xml. Analyzes on demand, like the SARIF export. An empty flowId means the current document in local mode.
post.summary: Export analysis results as JUnit XML

post.description: SARIF 2.1.0 report of the flow's analysis (GitHub Code Scanning and other SARIF consumers), sent as the attachment pad-analysis.sarif. Analyzes on demand (a fresh analysis records history, as analyze does). An empty flowId means the current document in local mode.
Returns a graph representation of the flow's execution path.
Returns the history and dependencies of a specific variable within the flow.

post.summary: Evaluate a flow against an inline policy
Evaluate a flow against a persisted policy
Get a single policy by ID
Save a named policy for an organization

post.description: Updates the configuration parameters for a specific analysis rule.
Enables or disables a specific analysis rule by ID.

get.description: Returns all available analysis rules and their current configuration, with each rule's stage (stable, preview), introducedIn and kind (block, flow, library; library rules are listed only where desktop folder analysis runs them).

parameters.description: Scope the catalog to an organisation the caller belongs to (org custom rules + overrides)
parameters.name: orgId

post.description: handleSuppressionInventory lists every inline `# pad-ignore` directive in the flow and marks stale ones (the suppressed rule no longer fires on the target block). Audited against the flow's org rule profile. Viewer access.

200.description: Suppression entries: line, rule, blockLabel, blockType, subflow, stale, reason

post.summary: Clear triage status for a finding
List finding triage statuses for a flow
Set triage status for a finding
Batch-set triage statuses for multiple findings

get.description: GDPR data-subject export: profile, owned flows (with content), settings, API tokens, the complete audit history, chat conversations on owned flows, the comments and triage decisions the user authored, organisation memberships and active sessions. Content other users authored on shared flows is out of scope.

post.description: Changes the password for the currently authenticated user.

handleAuthForgotPassword issues a password-reset token and emails its link. It always responds 200 with the same body whether or not the email exists, so the endpoint cannot be used to enumerate accounts.
Authenticates a user and returns access and refresh tokens.
Logs out the current user. In stateless JWT mode, this is primarily a client-side operation.

get.description: Returns information about the currently authenticated user.

put.description: handleAuthUpdateProfile lets a user set their own display name and avatar URL. Both fields are optional and may be cleared by sending an empty string.

Creates a new user account with email and password.
Re-sends the verification link for a registered, still-unverified address. Always returns 200 so the endpoint cannot be used to probe which emails exist.

delete.description: handleAuthSessionRevoke revokes one of the caller's own sessions (refresh tokens) by ID, e.g. to sign out a lost device.

get.description: handleSSOCallback receives the IdP redirect, validates state, exchanges the code for a verified identity, finds or creates the local user, and bounces the browser back to the SPA with a short-lived single-use exchange ticket in the URL fragment (fragments are not sent to servers or logged).

post.description: handleSSOExchange swaps a single-use SSO ticket for a regular token pair — the SSO equivalent of handleAuthLogin's response.

get.description: handleSSOInfo tells the SPA whether to render the SSO login button.

409.description: No password set — unlinking would lock the account

get.description: handleSSOStart begins the OIDC authorization-code flow: it stores the state/nonce/PKCE-verifier in an HttpOnly cookie and redirects the browser to the IdP.

get.summary: List API tokens for the current user

post.description: handleAuthVerifyEmail redeems an email-verification token and marks the user's email verified.
Signals the backend to start sending events for the specified stream ID.
Cancels an active streaming session.
Deletes the chat history for a specific flow and provider.
Delivers the user's approve/decline for an apply_fix proposal pending in one of the caller's chat streams. First decision wins; unknown or already-decided proposals return 404.
post.summary: Respond to a fix approval prompt

post.description: Retrieves the chat history for a specific flow and conversation key (the wire field is historically named `provider`). The body is an object — {messages: [...]} (always an array) plus activeStreamId when the caller has a stream on this conversation whose question is stored but whose answer is not yet (live, or finished and still being stored) — so a client that reloads mid-turn can re-attach via /api/chat/resume instead of losing the answer until another reload. The frontend still accepts the bare array older servers answered with.

Returns a preview of the context that will be sent to the AI provider: the system prompt, the context text, the user message, an estimate of their tokens and the model's context window. The model resolves as the turn's would: for provider azure-foundry a model registry id the caller cannot use is refused with 400 and code MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE.

400.description: Bad Request (code MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE: the Azure AI Foundry model is not available to the caller)

post.description: Reconnect to an in-flight AI stream and catch up on missed chunks.

Saves the chat history for a specific flow and provider. A message's modelLabel (the model's display name when it was sent) is stored clamped: NFC-normalised, control, bidi and zero-width characters dropped, whitespace collapsed, at most 64 characters.

Initiates a streaming chat session with an AI provider. The answer arrives on the event stream as chunk, tool, tool_result, done and error events. The done payload carries tokensIn, tokensOut and chunks, plus — when known — servedModel (the model that answered an alias such as an Azure AI Foundry deployment, router or agent) and inputCostPerM / outputCostPerM (the per-million-token rates the turn was billed at). An error payload carries message and, when classified, code (AI_BUDGET_EXCEEDED, PROVIDER_AUTH, PROVIDER_PERMISSION, PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED, MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE, …). For provider azure-foundry the model is a model registry id ("m/<entryId>"; "" for the server default; a pre-registry deployment, "claude:" or "agent:" id still resolves for one release): one the caller cannot use — removed, another owner's, no longer shared with them — is refused before any stream starts with 400 and code MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE.

400.description: Bad Request (code MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE: the Azure AI Foundry model is not available to the caller)

429.description: Too many concurrent chat streams (code CHAT_CAPACITY_REACHED)

post.description: Returns suggested prompts based on the current flow state.

get.description: Every section is computed for the same scope and window. Findings filters (severity, category, rule) map each flow's per-rule counts through the current rule catalog.
get.summary: Filterable analytics for the Analytics page

parameters.description: IANA time zone for day bucketing (default UTC)
parameters.name: tz

get.summary: Aggregated dashboard data for the home view

get.description: Long-lived SSE channel for analysis, chat, and collaboration events. Chunks stream incrementally; reconnect with Last-Event-ID to resume.

post.description: Returns a diff between the currently loaded flow and a flow at the specified path. Only available in local mode.

Renders the flow's current analysis report as a self-contained HTML page and returns it base64-encoded under `data`. Needs a report (409 until the flow was analyzed). On the desktop a `path` also writes the file there; with accounts the path is ignored.

Renders the flow's current analysis report as Markdown and returns it base64-encoded under `data`. Needs a report (409 until the flow was analyzed). On the desktop a `path` also writes the file there; with accounts the path is ignored.

Renders the flow's current analysis report as a PDF and returns it base64-encoded under `data`. Needs a report (409 until the flow was analyzed). On the desktop a `path` also writes the file there; with accounts the path is ignored.
Desktop only. Writes the findings panel's CSV, or the SARIF / JUnit text it fetched, to the absolute path chosen in the native save dialog (.csv, .sarif or .xml only). 403 in cloud mode.

handleApplyFix applies a deterministic auto-fix (e.g. wrap-in-error-handler) to a block in the flow's source file, re-parses, and returns the updated document. Desktop/local only. The finding carries the available fixType in its AutoFix field; the frontend shows "Apply fix" only when that is set.

handleApplyFixBatch applies multiple auto-fixes in one pass (iterative loop, persisted once). The frontend's bulk-action bar derives the rule set from the selected findings; the server fixes every auto-fixable finding whose rule is in that set (re-parsing between fixes so line shifts don't corrupt targets).

post.summary: Move a block relative to another

post.description: Clears the entire list of recently opened flow documents.
Loads a flow document from the specified local folder path. Only available in local mode.
Loads a flow document from the specified local file path. Only available in local mode.

handlePreviewFix returns the before/after source text for a fix WITHOUT writing. The frontend renders a diff so the user can review the change before committing. Works in both desktop (local source file) and cloud (stored raw source) modes for single-file flows.

get.description: Returns a list of recently opened flow documents.

post.description: handleReimport re-reads the currently-loaded flow's source file (desktop), re-parses it, and returns the fresh document — so a user who fixed something in Power Automate Desktop can re-import + re-analyze in one click without navigating the file picker. Uses doc.FilePath (the already-loaded path), so there's no path-injection surface. Cloud flows have no on-disk source → 403.
Removes a file from the list of recently opened flow documents.
Opens the system file manager at the specified path. Only available in local mode.
handleSaveSource replaces the flow's raw source text (from the in-app source editor), re-parses, and returns the updated document. Editor access.
Performs a search for text or patterns within a specific flow document.

handleSearchLibrary runs a query across every flow the caller can access (cross-flow / org-wide search), merging per-flow hits into one result set. Each hit is stamped with its source flowId/flowName so the UI can group them.

post.summary: Create a public share link for a flow
List active share links for a flow

get.description: handleGetSource returns the raw PAD source text for the flow. Desktop: reads the file (folder flows: the member named by ?file=, Main.txt when omitted). Cloud: returns the stored source. Viewer access.

parameters.description: Member file of a folder flow (bare filename)
parameters.name: file

400.description: Bad Request (file is not a member of the flow folder)

get.description: Returns a list of source files related to the current flow.

post.description: handleSuppressInSource writes a `# pad-ignore[ruleId]` directive into the flow's source file before the given block, re-parses, and returns the updated document. Desktop/local only — cloud flows have no on-disk source. This is the first end-to-end apply-fix: the suppression travels with the file (honored by the analyzer, CLI gate, baselines, CI), unlike a UI-only suppression.

get.description: Returns a list of users who have access to the specified flow. Any user with at least viewer access to the flow can view its collaborators.

Returns 200 when downstream dependencies (DB) are reachable, 503 otherwise.

post.description: Analyzes a stored flow for a CI runner. Authenticated by an HMAC-SHA256 of "<X-Baki-Timestamp>." + body under PAD_CI_WEBHOOK_SECRET, sent as X-Baki-Signature: sha256=<hex>; the timestamp must be within 5 minutes. Body: {flowId, failOn, format}. failOn is error (default), warning, info or none; findings of preview rules never fail the gate and are counted in `preview`. format "summary" (default) returns {flowId, flowName, passed, gate, errors, warnings, info, preview}, "report" adds the findings, "sarif" returns the SARIF 2.1.0 document instead (application/sarif+json).

200.description: Gate verdict, or the SARIF document

401.description: Missing or invalid signature or timestamp

post.description: handleInviteAccept redeems an invite token, adding the calling user to the invite's organisation with the role specified in the invite.

Deletes an API key for a given provider. For azure-foundry (deprecated form, one release): removes the caller's resource "default" — the migrated single-document configuration — with its models and its stored credential; the other resources stay (DELETE /api/providers/azure-foundry/connections/{connectionId} removes one).

Checks if an API key for a given provider is saved. For azure-foundry (deprecated form, one release): whether the caller has at least one Azure AI Foundry resource of their own — GET /api/providers/azure-foundry/connections lists them.
Saves an API key for a given provider.

Creates a new organization owned by the caller, who becomes its

get.summary: List pending invites for an organization

post.description: handleOrgInviteCreate creates a pending invite for an email to join the organisation. Only org admins may create invites. The raw invite token is returned exactly once in this response — only its hash is persisted, so it cannot be recovered later. The caller is responsible for delivering it to the invitee (e.g. via an emailed accept link).

Re-embeds every knowledge chunk with the caller's embedding provider — the recovery path after switching embedding provider/model, which strands the existing corpus at the old dimension (searches silently return nothing). When the corpus was indexed with a different embedding model at the same width, the request is refused with 409 EMBEDDING_MODEL_CHANGED unless the body sets "force": true — re-indexing switches every document to the caller's model, and members whose embedding provider uses another model stop receiving the org's guidelines.

parameters.description: Optional. force=true re-indexes even when the corpus was indexed with a different embedding model (first request of a run only); cursor = the previous answer's nextCursor resumes the run after it
parameters.name: request

200.description: Re-indexed this request's pages ({chunks, docs}); nextCursor (with truncated=true) means chunks remain — post again with {force, cursor: nextCursor}. Every page is committed as it completes, so a later failure keeps the earlier pages — a request that FAILS after committing pages answers its error code with details {nextCursor, chunks} to resume from

400.description: Embedding provider not configured (EMBEDDING_NOT_CONFIGURED; EMBEDDING_ORG_NOT_CONFIGURED when the org's shared Azure credential names no embedding deployment), rejected credentials (EMBEDDING_AUTH_FAILED, EMBEDDING_PERMISSION_DENIED), a request the provider rejected (EMBEDDING_PROVIDER_REJECTED) or malformed body / cursor

409.description: Embedding model differs from the indexed corpus (EMBEDDING_MODEL_CHANGED; resend with force — on a resumed request: the caller's model is not the one the run converted to) or another upload/re-index of this org is in flight (KNOWLEDGE_BUSY)

429.description: Embedding provider throttled the request (EMBEDDING_RATE_LIMITED) or the daily AI budget is spent (BUDGET_EXCEEDED)

503.description: Embedding provider unavailable (EMBEDDING_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE) or the budget could not be checked (BUDGET_UNAVAILABLE)

504.description: The request's deadline ran out before a page was committed (KNOWLEDGE_TIMEOUT)

post.description: Chunks and embeds the document with the caller's embedding provider. Refused with 409 EMBEDDING_MODEL_CHANGED when that provider's model is not the one the org's knowledge base was indexed with (mixing models would make documents unfindable for members on the other model).

400.description: Embedding provider not configured (EMBEDDING_NOT_CONFIGURED; EMBEDDING_ORG_NOT_CONFIGURED when the org's shared Azure credential names no embedding deployment), rejected credentials (EMBEDDING_AUTH_FAILED, EMBEDDING_PERMISSION_DENIED) or a request the provider rejected (EMBEDDING_PROVIDER_REJECTED)

409.description: Embedding model differs from the indexed corpus (EMBEDDING_MODEL_CHANGED) or another upload/re-index of this org is in flight (KNOWLEDGE_BUSY)

413.description: The document chunks to more passages than one upload may index (KNOWLEDGE_DOCUMENT_TOO_LARGE)

delete.description: Removes a user from an organization. Only organization admins can remove members.

200.description: OK; sharedCredentialDisabled is true when the removed member was the lender of the org's shared Azure AI Foundry credential and it was disabled
Updated; sharedCredentialDisabled is true when the demoted member was the lender of the org's shared Azure AI Foundry credential and it was disabled

get.description: Deprecated (one release): use GET /api/orgs/{id}/providers/azure-foundry/connections and /models. Returns the org's resource "default" (the single-document configuration it migrated to) without any secret: endpoint, auth mode, whether a secret is stored, the Entra ID tenant and client IDs, the project endpoint and the deployment names — built from the registry's entries of that resource, never from the stored document's old fields — plus who shared it (updatedBy: the display name, else email, of the admin who supplied the stored secret — an edit by another admin that kept the secret does not change it) and when it was last saved (updatedAt: RFC 3339 with sub-second precision — send it back verbatim as the save's compare-and-swap token). Any member, viewers included (only admins and members run on it). {configured:false, shared:false} when the org has none; 500 ORG_CREDENTIAL_UNREADABLE when it has one that cannot be read (a deployment key rotation, a database failure).
get.summary: Get the organisation's shared Azure AI Foundry configuration

404.description: Unknown org, or no org keystore in this deployment (ORG_KEYSTORE_UNAVAILABLE)

500.description: The stored configuration cannot be read (ORG_CREDENTIAL_UNREADABLE)

post.description: Deprecated (one release): use the org registry routes (POST/PUT /api/orgs/{id}/providers/azure-foundry/connections, /models). Validates and stores the org's shared Azure AI Foundry endpoint, credential (API key or Microsoft Entra ID service principal), optional project endpoint and deployment names as its resource "default": the credential part is saved (the stored document's old deployment fields carried over unchanged, for a rolled-back binary) and the deployment fields are mapped onto that resource's models — missing ones added, removed ones deleted. Org admins only. An omitted secret keeps the stored one only while the endpoint host (and the project endpoint's host) is unchanged — a changed endpoint needs the secret re-entered (MISSING_SECRET); the admin who supplies the secret becomes the credential's lender (it is disabled when they stop being an admin), an edit that keeps it does not. The body must be exactly one JSON object with known fields only (INVALID_CONFIG otherwise). Compare-and-swap: send back the updatedAt the GET returned (omit it only when the GET said configured:false); when the stored configuration changed since — another admin saved or removed it — nothing is written and the answer is 409 CONFLICT (reload, then re-apply). The reply's updatedAt is the token for the next save.
post.summary: Save the organisation's shared Azure AI Foundry configuration

parameters.description: The configuration plus the updatedAt it was loaded with
parameters.name: request

400.description: INVALID_CONFIG, INVALID_ENDPOINT, INVALID_PROJECT_ENDPOINT, INVALID_AUTH, MISSING_SECRET, MISSING_DEPLOYMENT, INVALID_DEPLOYMENT, CONFIG_TOO_LARGE or HOST_NOT_ALLOWED

404.description: Unknown org, or no org keystore in this deployment (ORG_KEYSTORE_UNAVAILABLE)

409.description: The stored configuration changed since it was loaded (CONFLICT), or the organisation's resource or model limit (TOO_MANY_CONNECTIONS, TOO_MANY_MODELS)

post.description: Deprecated (one release): use POST/PUT /api/providers/azure-foundry/connections and /models. Validates and stores the caller's Azure AI Foundry endpoint, credential (API key or Microsoft Entra ID service principal), optional project endpoint and deployment names as their resource "default": the credential part is saved (the stored document's old deployment fields carried over unchanged, for a rolled-back binary) and the deployment fields are mapped onto that resource's models — missing ones added, removed ones deleted. An omitted secret keeps the stored one while the endpoint host is unchanged. The body must be exactly one JSON object with known fields only (INVALID_CONFIG otherwise).

get.description: The caller's Azure AI Foundry resources ("connections"; the UI calls them resources), then — read-only, marked shared with orgId and orgName — the resources of every organisation where the caller is an admin or member (admins change those through the org routes). Each carries its public settings (never a secret, never deployment fields), its status computed at read time (ready, needs_credentials, unreadable, invalid_config, with statusReason) and its last test. registryState is ok, read_only (the desktop list file was written by a newer app version: writes answer 409 REGISTRY_READ_ONLY) or recovered (a corrupt list file was set aside; recoveredCopyPath says where); limits are the per-owner caps; knowledgeEmbeddingEnabled says whether "Use for knowledge base" is offered. Never waits on the network.

post.description: Validates and stores a resource: a name (1 to 64 characters; empty takes the endpoint host's first label) and its settings — the endpoint, the credential (an API key, a Microsoft Entra ID service principal or, on the desktop, the Azure CLI sign-in) and an optional Foundry project endpoint (discovery and agents). No deployment fields: models are added with POST /models. The body must be exactly one JSON object with known fields only, at most 64 KiB (400 INVALID_CONFIG otherwise). Audited (azure.connection_save, op create).

post.description: Registers a deployment (kind chat, claude or embedding) or a project agent (kind agent: its resource needs Entra ID and a project endpoint, else 400 KIND_REQUIRES_PROJECT) on one of the caller's resources, with an optional display name (the deployment name by default), purpose (general by default, or custom with purposeCustom), description, context window and output cap. isKnowledgeEmbedding makes an embedding model the knowledge base's (where the knowledge base embeds with Azure); on a non-empty corpus that is 409 REINDEX_REQUIRED unless force is true. isDefault is for organisations only. Strict body, at most 16 KiB. Audited (azure.model_save, op create).

chatDeployment.description:
ChatDeployment is the deployment offered as the default model; EmbeddingDeployment (optional) the
knowledge-base one; Deployments (≤ azureMaxDeployments) further chat deployments — an API-key caller's
deployments are not listable, so the picker shows exactly these names. Saving requires a chat deployment
unless the project listing can supply one (MISSING_DEPLOYMENT).

claudeDeployments.description:
ClaudeDeployments (≤ azureMaxClaudeDeployments) answer on the Anthropic Messages route
({endpoint}/anthropic/v1/messages), not /openai/v1 (404); offered as "claude:<name>" and also discovered
by the project listing (modelPublisher "Anthropic").

endpoint.description: Endpoint is the resource endpoint, e.g. https://my-res.openai.azure.com or https://my-res.services.ai.azure.com (no path).

projectEndpoint.description:
ProjectEndpoint (optional) is the Foundry project endpoint, https://<res>.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/<project>,
which unlocks the project's agents (Entra ID only) and deployment metadata.

contextWindow.description:
ContextWindow is the STORED window in tokens, omitted when unset (the
provider then uses LocalDefaultContextWindow, 8192).

activeStreamId.description:
ActiveStreamID is the caller's stream whose answer is not yet stored (live, or finished and
still being stored); omitted once the answer is stored.

chatDeployment.description:
ChatDeployment is the deployment offered as the default model; EmbeddingDeployment (optional) the
knowledge-base one; Deployments (≤ azureMaxDeployments) further chat deployments — an API-key caller's
deployments are not listable, so the picker shows exactly these names. Saving requires a chat deployment
unless the project listing can supply one (MISSING_DEPLOYMENT).

ClaudeDeployments (≤ azureMaxClaudeDeployments) answer on the Anthropic Messages route
({endpoint}/anthropic/v1/messages), not /openai/v1 (404); offered as "claude:<name>" and also discovered
by the project listing (modelPublisher "Anthropic").

fixProposal.description:
FixProposal snapshots the single apply_fix approval record — LEGACY,
superseded by FixProposals; kept for pre-migration conversations.

fixProposals.description:
FixProposals snapshots every apply_fix/apply_fixes approval record: a
stream can carry several sequential proposals, a batch several fixes.

servedModel.description:
ServedModel is the model that actually answered when Model is a resolvable
alias, and Input/OutputCostPerM the USD per 1M rates billed — all from the
stream's done event, so a reloaded conversation prices the turn at what it
cost. Zero/empty = not reported.

toolCalls.description: ToolCalls records the tool invocations behind this assistant message.

name.description: Name is the resource's display name; "" takes the endpoint host's first label.

credentialUpdatedAt.description: CredentialUpdatedAt (org scope): the CAS on the org's stored credential.

dismissDiscovery.description: DismissDiscovery hides (true) or brings back (false) the "Found in your project" prompt.

force.description: Force confirms the re-index an endpoint change of the KB model's resource needs (else 409 REINDEX_REQUIRED).

updatedAt.description: UpdatedAt is the resource's last-read updatedAt: a stale value is 409 CONFLICT.

canDiscover.description: CanDiscover and SupportsAgents: Entra ID (or the Azure CLI) with a project endpoint.

credentialUpdatedAt.description: CredentialUpdatedAt (org scope) is the stored credential's compare-and-swap token.

legacy.description: Legacy marks the resource the single-document configuration became.

name.description: Name is the resource's display name (1–64 characters).

shared.description: Shared marks an organisation's resource: org scope always, user scope read-only ("Shared with you").

sharedBy.description: SharedBy names who lent a shared resource's credential (display name, else email); SharedByID is that admin's id.

suggestDiscovery.description: SuggestDiscovery shows the "Found in your project" prompt when discoverable and not dismissed.

updatedAt.description: UpdatedAt is the registry row's compare-and-swap token (RFC 3339).

recoveredCopyPath.description: RecoveredCopyPath is where the recovered desktop list file's copy was kept (recovered only).

registryState.description: RegistryState is ok, read_only (a newer app wrote the desktop list file) or recovered (a corrupt one set aside, copy kept).

alreadyAdded.description: AlreadyAdded: the resource registers it already, as ModelID.

deployment.description: Deployment (agents) is the project deployment the agent runs on; Workflow marks a workflow agent.

kind.description: Kind is what it would be added as: chat, claude or embedding for a deployment, agent for an agent.

model.description: Model is the model behind it ("" when unknown).

contextWindow.description:
ContextWindow and MaxOutputTokens are optional overrides (0 = none;
never on an embedding model).

displayName.description: DisplayName defaults to the deployment name; Purpose to general.

force.description:
Force confirms the re-index a new knowledge-base model needs on a
non-empty corpus (else 409 REINDEX_REQUIRED).

isDefault.description:
IsDefault (org scope only) = the organisation's "Default for members";
IsKnowledgeEmbedding (embedding model, KB embeds with Azure) = the KB's model.

contextWindow.description:
ContextWindow and MaxOutputTokens: null clears the override; the
swaggertype tags document the integer-or-null wire form (OptionalInt).

force.description:
Force confirms the re-index a knowledge-base change needs on a
non-empty corpus (else 409 REINDEX_REQUIRED).

isDefault.description:
IsDefault / IsKnowledgeEmbedding: true moves the designation to this
model, false clears it from it.

purpose.description:
Purpose: a preset clears the stored custom text; "custom" takes
PurposeCustom (or keeps the stored text).

updatedAt.description:
UpdatedAt, when sent, is the model's updatedAt as last read
(compare-and-swap: a stale value is 409 CONFLICT).

contextWindow.description: ContextWindow/MaxOutputTokens are the user's overrides; ReportedContextWindow is the server-known window.

deployment.description: Deployment is the deployment name, or the agent's name.

target.description: Target is what the server routes to: "<deployment>", "claude:<deployment>" or "agent:<name>".
